paths.description: Entry and character/game explanation template; covers initial purpose, support disclosure, responsive behavior, network, security, discoverability, and preferences.
Distinct interactive 4-panel manga carousel template; covers gesture behavior, content imagery, mobile rendering, and route metadata.
Distinct social-links template; covers named links, external destinations, mobile rendering, and route metadata.
Mobile-user-agent handoff reached by the entry journey; covers the primary authentication flow and input assistance.

findings.summary: The page ignores the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark screenshot is pixel-equivalent to the default capture and the platform probe reports colorScheme "normal" with no dark-theme treatment.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-aware surface, text, and control colors.

findings.summary: Navigation changes have no transition continuity.
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS inspection found no view-transition declarations across the three full-page content routes.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a restrained cross-document view transition, with reduced-motion fallback, for the shared header and content frame.

findings.summary: Long pages provide no scroll-position guidance.
findings.evidence: The mobile home capture is several screens tall, while DOM/CSS evidence shows neither sticky progress/navigation nor scroll-state feedback.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep section navigation available or add a subtle progress/position affordance for long content.

findings.summary: The expandable support notice is mouse-only custom UI.
findings.evidence: The probe identifies .noticeHead as an H2 and .close as a SPAN with no role or tabindex; both respond to click but are absent from keyboard navigation.
findings.suggestedFix: Use details/summary or buttons with expanded state, keyboard activation, and an accessible close control.

findings.summary: Mobile browsers receive a desktop canvas scaled down to 36.7%.
findings.evidence: At a 360x800 viewport, layout reports no viewport meta and a 980 CSS-pixel layout viewport; screenshots show tiny text and controls across home, manga, and SNS.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a standard viewport meta tag and rebuild the fixed desktop layout as a fluid, reflowing mobile layout.

findings.summary: Components do not adapt to their available width.
findings.evidence: The platform probe finds no container-query usage; fixed 768px content images and a 180px carousel margin are visible in rendered DOM.
findings.suggestedFix: Make the content frame and carousel intrinsically sized, then use container queries where component layout must change.

findings.summary: Input modality support is incomplete.
findings.evidence: The support disclosure controls are not keyboard focusable, and one page-top link computes outline:none while focused.
findings.suggestedFix: Use semantic controls and preserve a visible :focus-visible treatment for every interactive element.

findings.summary: The first viewport does not expose a clear primary action.
findings.evidence: The home screenshot presents branding and troubleshooting first; navigation labels are literally "test" and no named start/play action appears in the control inventory.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace placeholder labels and expose one clearly named play/start action with supporting device requirements.

findings.summary: The primary journey is fragmented across three redirects and a separate login origin.
findings.evidence: HAR records 302 -> 307 -> 302 before the content page, while Lighthouse with a mobile user agent lands on id.gree.net rather than the audited content URL.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a single canonical HTTPS entry route and make the play-to-login transition explicit and stable.

findings.summary: Loading performance misses the good LCP range.
findings.evidence: The raw-CDP trace reports FCP 3941.51ms and LCP 4193.03ms; Lighthouse’s redirected mobile journey is slower still and is retained only as corroboration for that journey.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove redirect latency, prioritize the true LCP asset, and defer non-critical scripts.

findings.summary: Resource delivery is delayed by redirects, parser-blocking assets, and third-party weight.
findings.evidence: HAR reports 36 requests/862,797 transferred bytes, three redirects, two VeryHigh parser stylesheets, and parser-inserted scripts without async/defer; trace load ends at 4501.54ms.
findings.suggestedFix: Eliminate redirect hops, inline only critical CSS, defer scripts, and set explicit loading priority for key assets.

findings.summary: Legacy and likely non-critical scripts inflate a mostly static page.
findings.evidence: HAR shows 231,293 script bytes including jQuery 1.11.1, LAB 2.0.3, analytics, and Tag Manager on a page whose only bespoke interaction is a disclosure toggle.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove obsolete loaders/dependencies and load analytics after consent or idle.

findings.summary: Important images, links, and controls lack accessible names.
findings.evidence: The image audit reports 6 of 7 images without alt; DOM shows empty SNS links and all three nav destinations named "test"; the custom disclosure controls have no roles.
findings.suggestedFix: Give meaningful images and links concise accessible names, mark decorative images with empty alt, and use native controls.

findings.summary: Document structure and focus handling exclude keyboard users.
findings.evidence: There is no main landmark in rendered markup; the notice H2/span controls cannot receive focus, and a focused page-top link has outline:none.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a main landmark, use logical heading structure, and ensure every action participates in a visible keyboard focus order.

findings.summary: Text is too small on mobile because the desktop page is scaled down.
findings.evidence: The 360px screenshots render the 980px fixed page at 0.367 scale, making sidebar and explanatory copy impractically small.
findings.suggestedFix: Use responsive typography and reflow, with readable line lengths and a true mobile viewport.

findings.summary: Mobile zoom/reflow expectations are not met.
findings.evidence: All three content templates omit viewport meta and render a desktop-width document in the mobile capture.
findings.suggestedFix: Add width=device-width, initial-scale=1 without disabling zoom, and make content reflow at narrow widths.

findings.summary: Image markup omits intrinsic dimensions and responsive delivery.
findings.evidence: The image primitive reports 7/7 images without width/height, 7/7 without srcset, 7 legacy PNGs, and 6 below-fold images without lazy loading.
findings.suggestedFix: Set intrinsic dimensions, lazy-load below-fold images, and provide appropriately compressed responsive sources.

findings.summary: The page uses fragile browser-platform patterns.
findings.evidence: DOM contains duplicate page-top IDs, javascript:void(0) navigation, HTTP internal hrefs, and mouse-only click handlers.
findings.suggestedFix: Use unique IDs, real HTTPS URLs, semantic buttons for actions, and progressive event handling.

findings.summary: Two representative content routes have empty titles and descriptions.
findings.evidence: manga-dom.json and sns-dom.json both report an empty document title and empty meta description.
findings.suggestedFix: Give each template a unique descriptive title and summary.

findings.summary: Navigation links are not descriptive and use insecure HTTP destinations.
findings.evidence: All three internal nav labels are "test" and their authored hrefs are http://jp.apps.gree.net/...; robots.txt and sitemap.xml both return 404.
findings.suggestedFix: Use descriptive HTTPS links and publish accurate robots and sitemap signals.

findings.summary: Share and structured metadata is stale or empty.
findings.evidence: Home og:url points to http://apps.gree.net/95, static routes emit empty Open Graph values, and the probe finds no JSON-LD.
findings.suggestedFix: Align canonical/Open Graph URLs to HTTPS, populate route metadata, and add schema.org data where it represents the game.

findings.summary: The document lacks baseline defensive response headers.
findings.evidence: Headers evidence reports missing CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, clickjacking protection, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy HSTS, a restrictive CSP with frame-ancestors, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, and a minimal Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: The page sends a disproportionate tracking footprint before any visible consent.
findings.evidence: Tracker evidence finds 10 third-party origins and Google Analytics, DoubleClick, Tag Manager, and UserHeat; HAR attributes 34/36 requests and 862,536 bytes to non-entry origins.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimize vendors, gate non-essential analytics on consent, batch events, and self-host essential assets where practical.

findings.summary: Failure handling falls back to generic server behavior.
findings.evidence: Both /robots.txt and /sitemap.xml return a bare server 404; the core entry journey also traverses several origins without an explanatory intermediate/retry state.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide branded, actionable HTTP failure states and retry guidance for the play/login handoff.

findings.summary: The login flow does not declare autofill purpose tokens.
findings.evidence: The login DOM shows email and password inputs without autocomplete=username and autocomplete=current-password.
findings.suggestedFix: Add correct autocomplete tokens and preserve password-manager/passkey compatibility.

findings.summary: Asset delivery is heavier than the static content warrants.
findings.evidence: Images account for 602,775 transferred bytes; all audited img elements are PNG without responsive sources, and six below-fold images load eagerly.
findings.suggestedFix: Use modern compressed responsive images and defer non-visible assets.

findings.summary: Background analytics work dominates a simple static page.
findings.evidence: Known trackers run across four domains and Tag Manager alone transfers 156,876 bytes; two analytics fetches fail/abort during capture.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer or remove non-essential measurement and avoid background work until consent and idle.

findings.summary: Third-party work consumes nearly the entire transfer budget.
findings.evidence: The HAR attributes 862,536 of 862,797 transferred bytes to origins other than the entry origin, including 178KB+ of analytics/tag scripts.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party byte/request budget and remove or delay vendors that do not support the primary task.

taskList.title: Ship a true responsive mobile layout with readable reflow and zoom
Make controls, links, images, and landmarks semantic and keyboard accessible
Simplify the canonical play-to-login path and improve LCP/resource priority
Add baseline security headers and reduce pre-consent tracking
Replace placeholder navigation and expose a clear primary action
Repair per-route title, description, Open Graph, and structured metadata
Modernize responsive image markup and lazy loading
